title: Cybersecurity dashboards: Transactional Activity, Advanced Threats, Sandbox Threats, Threat Locations and SSL Inspection

prose.text: {{time-range}} These are separate dashboards from the Cybersecurity Insights report in [[zia.reports.security]]; the ZIA predefined dashboards are in [[zia.insights]]. Whether they read the same data as Cybersecurity Insights is not stated {{gap:data-source}}.

prose.label: Incidents.
prose.text: {{incident-table}} {{incident-details}} The Advanced Threats details list repeats SHA-2 and Total Bytes {{gap:page-defects}}.

prose.label: Sandbox Threats.
prose.text: {{sandbox-threats}} {{sandbox-patient-zero}} The Sandbox Activity Report's reading in [[zia.reports.security:sandbox-activity-reading]] holds two of the three statements in {{sandbox-patient-zero|ref}}.

cybersecurity-widgets.statement: The Cybersecurity dashboard's widgets show transactions detected and blocked (toggling between Malicious Transactions and Policy Blocks), the top threat categories stopped, the countries where threats originate, the flow and dispensation of files sent to the sandbox, and SSL traffic that occurred and was inspected; links open the Transactional Activity, Advanced Threats, Threat Locations, Sandbox Threats and SSL Inspection dashboards.

quotes: This widget shows the cybersecurity transactions detected and blocked by Zscaler during the selected time period.
Click the toggle to switch between Malicious Transactions and Policy Blocks.
This widget shows the top threat categories stopped by Zscaler.
This widget shows the countries where threats are originating.
This widget shows the flow and dispensation of files sent to the sandbox.
This widget shows the SSL traffic that occurred and that was inspected.
Click View Transaction Activity to see more detail on the Transactional Activity Dashboard.
Click View All Advanced Threats to see all advanced threat activity on the Advanced Threats Dashboard.
Click View All Threat Locations to see more detail on the Threat Locations Dashboard.
Click View All Sandbox Threats to see more detail on the Sandbox Threats Dashboard.
Click View SSL Inspection to see more detail on the SSL Inspection Dashboard.

transactional-activity.statement: The Transactional Activity dashboard has Threats and Policy Blocks tabs: Threats charts malicious threats over the period and the top users and departments generating them; Policy Blocks charts transactions blocked for policy reasons, with widgets named Top Application Class, Top URL Categories Blocked, Top Cloud Applications Blocked and Top Blocked File Types.

quotes: The Transactional Activity page has two tabs: Threats and Policy Blocks.
This line graph shows the number of malicious threats for the selected time period.
This bar chart shows the users who generated the most threats in your organization and the number of threats generated.
This proportional area chart shows the departments that generated the most threats
This line graph shows the number of transactions that were blocked for policy reasons for the selected time period.
Top Application Class
Top URL Categories Blocked
Top Cloud Applications Blocked
Top Blocked File Types

advanced-threats.statement: The Advanced Threats dashboard (Cyberthreat Protection > Insights > Advanced Threats) provides an overview of cybersecurity threats and charts the incidents recorded for the period; its category selection includes or excludes threat categories, and Unknown represents incidents the service could not classify under a threat category or that were not classifiable under any of the preceding categories.

quotes: The Advanced Threats dashboard (Cyberthreat Protection > Insights > Advanced Threats) provides an overview of cybersecurity threats in your organization.
Select the threat categories you want to include or exclude in the line graph:
This line graph shows the number of incidents recorded for the selected time period.
Unknown (this represents all the incidents that the Zscaler service was unable to classify under a threat category or were not classifiable under any of the preceding categories)

advanced-threat-categories.statement: The Advanced Threat category selection lists Malware, Spyware, Virus, Sandbox Adware, Sandbox Anonymizer, Sandbox Malware, Sandbox Offensive Security Tools, Sandbox Ransomware, Suspected Spyware or Adware, Adware/Spyware Sites, Advanced Security, Botnet Callback, Browser Exploit, Crypto Mining, Domain Generated Algorithm Domains, Malicious Content, Suspicious Content, Peer-to-Peer, Phishing, Suspicious Destinations, Unauthorized Communication, Webspam, Cross-site Scripting and Unknown.

quotes: - Malware - Spyware - Virus - Sandbox Adware - Sandbox Anonymizer - Sandbox Malware - Sandbox Offensive Security Tools - Sandbox Ransomware - Suspected Spyware or Adware - Adware/Spyware Sites - Advanced Security - Botnet Callback

- Browser Exploit - Crypto Mining - Domain Generated Algorithm Domains - Malicious Content - Suspicious Content - Peer-to-Peer - Phishing - Suspicious Destinations - Unauthorized Communication - Webspam - Cross-site Scripting - Unknown

incident-table.statement: The Advanced Threat Incidents and Sandbox Incidents tables give each incident's Name, Category, Impacted Systems (the number of systems affected), Status (the action taken, for example Allowed or Blocked) and first and last known dates; clicking a row shows additional detail on two tabs.

quotes: Name: The name of the threat incident.
Category: The threat category (e.g. Spyware, Phishing, etc.)
Impacted Systems: The number of systems affected by the incident.
Status: The action taken on the threat (e.g., Allowed or Blocked).
Last Known Date: The date and time of the last known attempt by the threat.
First Known Date: The date and time of the first known attempt by the threat.
Click any row in the table to see additional detail on that advanced threat incident on two tabs:
Name: The name of the threat incident.
Category: The threat category (e.g. Sandbox Malware, Sandbox Adware, etc.)
Impacted Systems: The number of systems affected by the incident.
Status: The action taken on the threat, e.g. Allowed or Blocked.
Last Known Date: The date and time of the last known attempt by the threat.
First Known Date: The date and time of the first known attempt by the threat.
Click any row in the table to see additional detail on that sandbox threat incident on two tabs:

incident-details.statement: On the Sandbox Threats and Advanced Threats dashboards an incident's details include Policy Action, Event Type, Duration (between the first and last known attempt), Total Transactions, Total Bytes, the Sandbox Category (if the file is sent for sandbox analysis), the MD5 of the file that triggered the rule, SHA-2 (256-bit), Destination IP and URL Category, and the originating Client IP (the client device's address) and Client External IP (the client's internet gateway location IP), which the Impacted Systems tab shows.

quotes: Policy Action: The policy action enforced on transactions related to the incident.
Event Type: The type of threat event.
Duration: The duration between the first and last known attempt by the threat.
Total Transactions: The total number of transactions related to the threat.
Total Bytes: The total bytes of data for all the transactions related to the threat.
Sandbox Category: The name of the sandbox category, if the file is sent for sandbox analysis.
MD5: The MD5 hash for the file that triggered the rule.
SHA-2 (256-bit): The hash of identical files.
Destination IP: The destination IP.
URL Category: The URL category of the incident.
Client IP: The IP address from which the transaction originated. This is the IP address of the client device.
Client External IP: The internet gateway location IP address of the client.
The Impacted Systems tab has information about the systems and users affected by the threat:

sandbox-threats.statement: The Sandbox Threats dashboard shows Sandbox policy actions for known files (analyzed and classified malicious or benign) and unknown files (encountered for the first time), filterable by Status Allowed or Blocked; unknown-file verdicts are categorized as Allow & Scan, Quarantine and Allow/Do Not Scan.

quotes: The Sandbox Threats dashboard provides an overview of Sandbox policy actions taken for known and unknown files in your organization.
Known files are files that the Sandbox analyzed and classified as malicious or benign.
Unknown files are files that the Sandbox encounters for the first time.
Status: Select the result of the policy action: Allowed or Blocked.
This bar chart shows the number of benign or malicious files allowed or blocked for the selected time range.
Policy Actions & Verdicts for Unknown Files

This bar chart shows the number of files that were identified as benign or malicious after being sent for Sandbox analysis, categorized into three categories: Allow & Scan, Quarantine, and Allow/Do Not Scan.

sandbox-patient-zero.statement: A quarantined file could also be counted under Allow & Scan if it was allowed while in quarantine; malicious files downloaded due to the Allow & Scan policy action are patient 0 events, which Zscaler recommends investigating.

quotes: A situation might occur where a file that has been quarantined could also be counted under Allow & Scan if the file was allowed while in quarantine.
Malicious files downloaded due to the Allow & Scan policy action are patient 0 events.
Zscaler recommends investigating these files.

threat-locations.statement: The Threat Locations dashboard (Cyberthreat Protection > Insights > Threat Locations) can include or exclude geolocations and shows a choropleth map of threats by location, with a bar chart of the applications that generated the most threats.

quotes: The Threat Locations dashboard (Cyberthreat Protection > Insights > Threat Locations) provides an overview of the threats in your organization and the users and applications responsible for them.
Geolocation: Use this drop-down menu to include or exclude location data from the dashboard.
This choropleth map shows the number of threats to your organization by location in the specified time range.
This bar chart shows the applications that generated the most threats in your organization and the number of threats generated.

ssl-inspection.statement: The SSL Inspection dashboard shows threats blocked due to SSL inspection by application, and the applications, locations and URL categories with the most traffic for which SSL inspection is not enabled.

quotes: a circle chart indicating threats blocked due to SSL inspection, broken out by application.
This bar graph shows the applications with the most traffic for which you have not enabled SSL inspection, and the volume of traffic for those applications.
This bar graph shows the locations with the most traffic for which you have not enabled SSL inspection
This bar graph shows the URL categories with the most traffic for which you have not enabled SSL inspection

data-source.title: Whether these dashboards read the same data as Cybersecurity Insights, and their retention
data-source.detail: The dashboard pages give a 1 to 90 day range but no retention beyond it, and do not say whether they read the same data as the Cybersecurity Insights report.

page-defects.title: Page inconsistencies on the Cybersecurity dashboards
page-defects.detail: The Advanced Threats details list repeats SHA-2 and Total Bytes. Transactional Activity lists its four policy-block widget names apart from the descriptions, so names are not paired with descriptions here. Only the Advanced Threats and Threat Locations pages give a Cyberthreat Protection > Insights path.
